newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK protest uses pro-China daily's Tiananmen blast.
newsitem.headline: HK protest uses pro-China daily's Tiananmen blast.

text.p: Pro-democracy activists astonished legislators in Hong Kong on Wednesday by distributing a pro-China newspaper that condemned the 1989 Tiananmen Square killing as "bloody fascism."
Then recipients realised they were reading old copies of the China-backed Hong Kong daily, Wen Wei Po, printed at the time of the army's Beijing crackdown on civilian protesters.
The newspaper later reversed its stance and rejoined the official line blaming the slain, unarmed demonstrators after troops crushed the massed democracy protest in the Chinese capital.
Activists handed out the June 5, 1989, edition with the banner headline "Vehemently Condemn the Bloody Fascist Atrocity".

Legislators were lobbied before they entered the assembly to will debate a member's resolution urging "vindication" of the Tiananmen protests that China branded as subversive. The move was seen as a symbolic gesture only.

The daily, long a Beijing mouthpiece, carried a front page picture of twisted bodies lying among wrecked bicycles, a reminder of outrage felt in Hong Kong, even in the pro-China camp, after the Chinese army cracked down that June 4.
"To our dead patriotic compatriots in Beijing we pay our respects," the newspaper said in a statement signed "the entire staff of the Hong Kong Wen Wei Po".
The crackdown on the student-led democracy movement in Beijing severely rattled Hong Kong's confidence years ahead of its return to China's rule on July 1.
The outrage has faded, but thousands in the territory still gather on June 4 each year to commemorate the massacre.
Following the Tiananmen incident, China's mouthpiece publications in Hong Kong underwent a thorough purge and quickly resumed toeing Beijing's line.

Earlier this week, the Wen Wei Po in an editorial condemned the Hong Kong government for allowing Chai Ling, one of the student leaders at Tiananmen in 1989, to enter the territory on a private visit.
